title: Sprint 3 - Basic Data Insertion
description: Complete all MongoDB queries in this sprint.

tickets.title: Insert First Users
tickets.description:
Add five users to the system: 'alice_dev' (alice@email.com), 'bob_ops' (bob@email.com), 'charlie_ux' (charlie@email.com), 'david_qa' (david@email.com), and 'eve_mgr' (eve@email.com). For MongoDB, assign them custom `_id` values: 1 through 5 respectively to match the autoincrement IDs.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
INSERT INTO users (id, username, email) VALUES 
(1, 'alice_dev', 'alice@email.com'),
(2, 'bob_ops', 'bob@email.com'),
(3, 'charlie_ux', 'charlie@email.com'),
(4, 'david_qa', 'david@email.com'),
(5, 'eve_mgr', 'eve@email.com');
```
tasks: Add five users to the system: 'alice_dev' (alice@email.com), 'bob_ops' (bob@email.com), 'charlie_ux' (charlie@email.com), 'david_qa' (david@email.com), and 'eve_mgr' (eve@email.com). For MongoDB, assign them custom `_id` values: 1 through 5 respectively to match the autoincrement IDs.
learning_objectives: Use insertMany for inserting multiple documents.
common_mistakes: Using SQL INSERT INTO syntax or omitting the array brackets in insertMany.
hints: Use db.users.insertMany() and pass an array of documents.

solution.query.js:
db.users.insertMany([
  { _id: 1, username: "alice_dev", email: "alice@email.com" },
  { _id: 2, username: "bob_ops", email: "bob@email.com" },
  { _id: 3, username: "charlie_ux", email: "charlie@email.com" },
  { _id: 4, username: "david_qa", email: "david@email.com" },
  { _id: 5, username: "eve_mgr", email: "eve@email.com" }
])

tickets.title: Insert First Todos
tasks:
Assign a first batch of tasks (with `_id` values 1 through 9) to different users:
1. For Alice (`user_id = 1`): 'Setup database' (priority 3, status 'pending', no due date).
2. For Alice (`user_id = 1`): 'Design schema' (priority 1, status 'completed', due date in the past '2026-06-15').
3. For Alice (`user_id = 1`): 'Configure CI/CD' (priority 3, status 'cancelled', no due date).
4. For Bob (`user_id = 2`): 'Deploy production' (priority 1, status 'completed', due date in the past '2026-06-20').
5. For Bob (`user_id = 2`): 'Monitor disk usage' (priority 2, status 'pending', due date in the past '2026-06-25').
6. For Charlie (`user_id = 3`): 'Create wireframes' (priority 2, status 'completed', due date in the past '2026-06-10').
7. For David (`user_id = 4`): 'Write test cases' (priority 3, status 'pending', due date in the future '2026-07-25').
8. For Eve (`user_id = 5`): 'Project kickoff' (priority 1, status 'completed', due date in the past '2026-06-01').
9. For Eve (`user_id = 5`): 'Weekly sync' (priority 3, status 'pending', due date in the future '2026-07-30').

Note: To demonstrate MongoDB's flexible schema, omit the `due_date` field entirely in documents where it is not set (instead of using null).
common_mistakes: Omitting fields, spelling names incorrectly, or writing due_date: null instead of omitting it.
hints: Use db.todos.insertMany() and omit due_date where it is null/empty.

  { _id: 6, user_id: 3, title: "Create wireframes", priority: 2, due_date: new Date("2026-06-10"), status: "completed" },
  { _id: 7, user_id: 4, title: "Write test cases", priority: 3, due_date: new Date("2026-07-25"), status: "pending" },
  { _id: 8, user_id: 5, title: "Project kickoff", priority: 1, due_date: new Date("2026-06-01"), status: "completed" },
  { _id: 9, user_id: 5, title: "Weekly sync", priority: 3, due_date: new Date("2026-07-30"), status: "pending" }
